transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Yeah, um… I guess I’ve just been feeling really worn out most days. It’s probably not a huge thing, but even when I get a full night’s sleep, I wake up feeling like my body and my head are still kind of dragging, and then I have to get through my cashier shift like that. I just thought maybe I should finally ask about it, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I get a little discouraged sometimes, I guess, but I wouldn’t want to call it depressed if that’s not what it is. I don’t feel, like, sad all the time or anything. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

Yeah… I mean, maybe more than I should. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but my mind kind of jumps around a lot—like from money stuff, to the relative staying with us, to my wife being stressed, then church things I’m supposed to help with, and whether I’m messing something up at work. It’s not always for one clear reason, it just sort of keeps going, if that makes sense.
When the worrying starts, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah… I mean, I try to control it. I’ll tell myself, like, “Just pray on it,” or “Leave it alone, it’s probably fine.” And sometimes that helps a little, but a lot of times once one worry starts, it kind of rolls into the next thing. Then I’m thinking through every bad way the day could go, even if I know that’s not really helpful. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you often wake up during the night and have trouble getting back to sleep?

Yeah… somewhat. I mean, I do get tired and go to bed, but a lot of nights I just kind of lie there thinking through bills, my schedule at work, whether things at home are okay. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but even when I do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
Have you been worrying like this most days for at least six months?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, not every single minute or anything, but most days, yes. It’s been going on maybe about a year and a few months—since our older relative moved in with us. I kept thinking it would settle down, so I didn’t really count it that way, but… yeah, probably around a year and three months.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight or you can’t relax?

Um… I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t really think of myself as tense like that. Maybe I get a little tight in my shoulders sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s just from work or normal stuff. I wouldn’t want to make too much of it. Is that what you mean?
Have you been more irritable than usual lately?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I get a little short sometimes, like anyone would, but I haven’t noticed myself snapping at people a lot or anything. At least I don’t think so. If that makes sense.
Do you often have trouble concentrating because your mind feels preoccupied or goes blank?

Yeah… sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but at the register I can be looking right at the screen and still kind of lose track because I’m thinking about stuff at home or bills. Then I’ll have to recount the drawer, or I catch a small mistake and fix it. It’s not constant, but it does happen.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?

Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I can get a little… unsettled if there’s a lot going on, but I wouldn’t say I’m pacing around or unable to sit still or anything. I’m not sure if that counts as “keyed up,” though.
Do you get tired easily?

Yeah… I guess that’s actually a big part of why I came in. I don’t want to complain, because I know everyone gets tired, but I feel pretty worn out almost every day. Even if I get a full night’s sleep, I’ll wake up and my body and my head still feel like they’re dragging when I have to get ready for my cashier shift. Is that the kind of tired you mean?
Do you often feel on edge or unable to relax?

I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I’d say I’m unable to relax, exactly. I mean, I can sit and watch TV or something, but sometimes I guess it takes me a bit to settle down. But I don’t want to overstate it… I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by on edge.
If you weren’t worrying, do you think you would still have trouble sleeping?

Probably not as much, no. I mean, I do go to bed tired, but most nights my mind kind of keeps going—bills, my work schedule, whether everyone at home is okay. I eventually sleep, usually, but it doesn’t feel like I really settled down, if that makes sense. I wake up feeling like I didn’t get the benefit of it.
Has this worrying been interfering with your daily life?

A little, yeah… I mean, not like everything is falling apart or anything. But at work I’ve noticed I’m double-checking my cash drawer more because I’ve made some small mistakes, and I don’t want that to become a problem. And I’ve kind of cut back on volunteering at the food pantry, which I feel bad about, but I just don’t feel like I can keep up with everything right now. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Before this worrying started, were you already having trouble sleeping?

Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I’d have the occasional bad night like anyone, but most of this seems tied to when I get in bed and start going over bills, my work schedule, whether everyone at home is okay… that kind of thing. Even if I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down. Does that answer what you mean?
Aside from the nights when worry keeps your mind going, are you dissatisfied with your sleep?

I guess not really aside from that, no. I mean, I’m tired when I get into bed, and it’s mostly that my mind starts running through bills and my work schedule and whether everyone at home is okay. Even when I do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really settle. But I don’t think I’d call it a separate sleep problem, if that makes sense.
Do you feel tired more easily than you used to?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s actually part of why I came in. I feel worn out almost every day lately, like even if I technically get a full night’s sleep, my body and my head are still kind of dragging when I get up for my cashier shift. Is that the kind of tired you mean?
